clue.text: Swift race circuit, brown round the turn

indicators.note: the two outer pieces go round the letter for the turn, enclosing it between them

parts.note: a circuit of a track is a lap
tan is a light brown colour
a U-turn, so U stands for the turn

explanation.surface: A racing lap described: round the circuit, past the brown patch at the bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swift' is Jonathan Swift: the Laputans are the people of the flying island in Gulliver's Travels. 'round' makes the circuit and the brown enclose the turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Laputans are the inhabitants of Laputa, a nation invented by Jonathan Swift in Gulliver's Travels.

clue.text: In bed -a bit of ear trouble has arisen

parts.note: the lobe is the soft lower part of the ear

indicators.note: in a down clue arising means going upwards, so the word for trouble is read from the bottom

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Someone laid up with an earache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In bed' sounds like a patient, but it is a flower in a garden bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobelia is a garden bedding plant with small blue flowers, typically grown in flowerbeds.

clue.text: Had final stroke on green and died

explanation.surface: An old croquet player who passed away on the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: In croquet a player finishes by striking the ball against the central stake; and slang for having passed away.

clue.text: Colour up, for example, when carrying the can

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters for for example are read from the bottom

parts.note: eg abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A face flushing as someone is caught holding the can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when carrying' only joins the pieces: TIN is followed by GE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinge is a slight trace of a hue, a tint.

clue.text: Novel by Scott, say, captures the style of the scientist

indicators.note: the outer pieces take the word for style prisoner, holding it inside them

parts.note: novel means new
Ian is a typical name for a Scot, and Scott's namesake: a Scotsman, say
ton means fashion or style

explanation.surface: A novel by Walter Scott capturing the manner of a famous scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scott' suggests Sir Walter, but a Scot, say, is IAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Newtonian means relating to Isaac Newton, the physicist, or his laws.

clue.text: Rather annoyed — the draught-excluder is hard to assemble

parts.note: in the game of draughts (checkers), to huff is to remove an opponent's piece that failed to capture, excluding it from play
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A DIY job: the strip that keeps out cold air is a pain to put together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draught-excluder' suggests a strip against cold air, but it is a player of draughts who huffs, taking off an opponent's piece. 'to assemble' just joins the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Huffish describes someone in a mild sulk, a little offended or petulant.

clue.text: Weeded round first of the seedlings and watered

indicators.note: the word for weeded goes round the picked letter, enclosing it

parts.note: to hoe is to weed with a hoe

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of seedlings

explanation.surface: A gardener's routine: weed among the young plants, then give them water.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosed means sprayed with water from a garden hose.

clue.text: Perhaps -saw every inch, complainingly

parts.note: to fret is to cut fretwork with a fretsaw, one way of sawing
every inch means completely, fully

explanation.surface: A carpenter sawing every inch while grumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: Fretfully means in an irritable, anxious, querulous way.

clue.text: Visions swaying around a lido

indicators.note: swaying around suggests the letters of a lido moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: Shimmering mirages around a swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Idola (plural of idolum) are phantoms or false mental images, in Bacon's philosophy fallacies.

clue.text: Embarrassing situation in excited constituency

parts.note: hot means excited or passionate
a seat in Parliament is a constituency

explanation.surface: An awkward moment in a fiercely contested election district.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the hot seat means facing tough questioning or difficult responsibility.

clue.text: Start being rebellious

indicators.note: rebellious letters refuse to stay in order, so the word being is rearranged

explanation.surface: A youth's first steps into revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: To start something is to commence it; both verbs mean set going.

clue.text: Scrubbed colourless

explanation.surface: A garment that has been laundered too often.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrubbed in the sense of cancelled, as a match rained off; and faded, pale and lacking colour.

clue.text: Belgian town chief to whom duty was owed

parts.note: Liège is a city in eastern Belgium
a lord is a chief or master

explanation.surface: A local leader in a Belgian town who commanded feudal loyalty.
explanation.definitionFit: In feudal society a vassal owed service and allegiance to his overlord.

clue.text: Make wrong charge for picture

explanation.surface: An art dealer overcharging for a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: To set someone up on a false accusation; and a single image, as one shot in a film reel.

clue.text: Notice decorated brickwork

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
the OBE (Order of the British Empire) is a British honour, so someone decorated may hold one

explanation.surface: A notice about honoured brickwork, perhaps on a listed building.
explanation.definitionFit: Adobe is sun-dried clay brick, or building work made from it.

clue.text: Cutter has cargo of gold, so he gets rid of spirits

indicators.note: a cutter is also a ship, and its cargo sits inside it, so gold goes inside

parts.note: an exciser is one who cuts out
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A ship carrying gold whose captain throws out the rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutter' looks like a boat, which fits 'cargo', but it is one who excises; 'spirits' looks like drink but means ghosts.
explanation.definitionFit: An exorciser drives out evil spirits or demons from a person or place.

clue.text: Ready to overlook the faults in dim-sounding chap

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the word for dim is only heard, not spelt in full, so its letters follow the sound

parts.note: dim and dull both mean slow-witted
a gent is a chap, a man

explanation.surface: Someone too forgiving of a slow-witted fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, IN DULL GENT is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An indulgent person is lenient and tolerant, willing to excuse failings.

clue.text: Apprised about a collision, vanish from the scene

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of apprised plus a are moved around

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Told of a crash, someone flees the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collision' adds to the surface, the letters colliding into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: To disappear is to go out of sight, to be lost to view.

clue.text: .Girl has nothing to talk about, so fade away

parts.note: Eva is a girl's name

indicators.note: the word for talking goes about the letter for nothing, enclosing it

parts.note: to prate is to talk foolishly
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A girl with nothing to say drifts off.
explanation.definitionFit: Evaporate means vanish, disappear as liquid turns to vapour.

clue.text: Expenditure for expeditions

explanation.surface: A budget heading for travel costs.
explanation.definitionFit: Money paid out, as costs; and trips out, excursions or journeys.

clue.text: Late extra expected to arrive.

parts.note: over means extra, left over
a train due is expected

explanation.surface: An extra train is expected but running late.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdue means past the expected time, tardy.

clue.text: Indeed a way used 'to get a rise

parts.note: yea is an old word for yes, indeed
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Asking for a pay rise by a certain route.
explanation.definitionFit: Bakers add this fungus to dough so that it ferments and swells up.

clue.text: Not time for Josephine to say Sir?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: say tells you the word for Sir is used only for its sound

parts.note: Sir is the title of a knight

explanation.surface: Napoleon's legendary rebuff to his wife, put as a riddle.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is 'Not tonight, Josephine', said to be Napoleon's line to Josephine; the answer is the missing word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonight names a particular time: this evening, the coming night.

clue.text: Rules of conduct seen even here in ancient Rome

parts.note: et is Latin for and or even, the language of ancient Rome
hic is Latin for here (or this)

explanation.surface: A moral code still visible today in the ruins of Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in ancient Rome' tells you both words are to be put into Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a set of moral principles governing behaviour.

clue.text: Without using his eyes, they say Houdini could conjure up a dog

indicators.note: conjure up suits a magician: the remaining letters are rearranged into a new word
without using means the letters named after it are left out of Houdini

parts.note: eyes sounds like Is, the two letter Is in the name

explanation.surface: Houdini performing a blindfold trick to produce a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: Houdini was a famous escapologist. Removing both Is leaves HOUDN, rearranged by 'could conjure up'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hound is a dog, especially one used for hunting.

clue.text: Island a hard place for a goat

parts.note: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples
a corn is a hard patch of skin on the foot

explanation.surface: Rocky Capri is a tough spot for a goat to live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a hard place' reads like rough terrain, but it is a corn on the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: The zodiac sign and constellation is pictured as a goat, often with a fish's tail.

clue.text: Near where Newbolt remarked on a breathless hush

definitions.text: where Newbolt remarked on a breathless hush

explanation.surface: A poem's tense cricket scene recalled.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Newbolt's poem Vitai Lampada begins 'There's a breathless hush in the Close tonight': the Close is a school cricket field.
explanation.definitionFit: Close as an adjective means nearby; and an enclosed school field, as in the poem.

clue.text: Computer data turned up in in-tray at the top

indicators.note: in tells you the turned letters go inside the others

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: at the top picks the opening letter of tray
turned means the two letters of up are flipped round

explanation.surface: Paperwork turned upside down in the office tray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' flips the little word, and the first 'in' sends it inside the word built from 'in-tray at the top'.
explanation.definitionFit: Input is information fed into a computer.

clue.text: Apothecary's place where the heroine, say, is locked up

parts.note: heroine sounds like heroin, an example of a drug
a store is a place where goods are kept locked away

explanation.surface: A thriller where the heroine is imprisoned in a pharmacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heroine' is a sound-alike for heroin, a drug; the store is where it is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A drugstore is an American-style chemist's shop, the modern pharmacist's premises.

clue.text: Summoned after parking accident

indicators.note: after says the word for summoned comes behind the parking letter

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
to ring for someone is to summon them

explanation.surface: Someone called out to a minor car-park collision.
explanation.walkthrough: PRANG is British slang for a minor crash, especially in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A prang is a minor crash or collision, usually involving a vehicle.

clue.text: To confirm, say which place. leads to' Kent

parts.note: said aloud, which is witch: the Witch of Endor in the Bible, so the witch's place is Endor
SE, the south-east, is the region Kent lies in, and London's SE postal district is the way into Kent

explanation.surface: A traveller seeking confirmation of the road to Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'which' stands for its sound-alike 'witch': the Witch of Endor was consulted by Saul in the Old Testament. Kent is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse is to approve or ratify, giving formal backing.

clue.text: Fall back in the sanatorium

explanation.surface: A patient collapsing back in hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw, as an army giving ground; and a secluded refuge where people go to recover, such as a rest home.
